question: Galvanisation is a method of protecting steel and iron from rusting by coating them with a thin layer of:
solution:
The correct answer is __**zinc**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galvanisation** is a specific metallurgical process used to protect **steel** and **iron** from **rusting** by applying a thin protective coating of **zinc**.
 
• The process works on the principle of **sacrificial protection**; because **zinc** is more chemically active than **iron**, it oxidizes in preference to the **iron** or **steel** it covers. ***Hence, the option zinc is correct.***
 
• Even if the **zinc** coating is scratched or damaged, the remaining **zinc** continues to act as a **sacrificial anode**, protecting the exposed **iron** from corrosion.
 
• The most common method is **hot-dip galvanizing**, where the metal parts are submerged in a bath of molten **zinc** at a temperature of approximately **450°C** (**842°F**).
 
• Other metals like **aluminium**, **copper**, and **magnesium** are not used in the process officially defined as "galvanisation." While **aluminium** provides corrosion resistance, it is used in processes like **anodizing** or as an alloy coating. ***Hence, statements involving aluminium, copper, and magnesium are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Rusting of Iron:** 
 
 
• **Rust** is a reddish-brown flaky substance formed when **iron** reacts with **oxygen** and **moisture** (water) in the environment.
 
• The chemical formula for **rust** is typically represented as **hydrated iron(III) oxide** (**Fe2O3·nH2O**).
 
• Both **air** and **water** are essential conditions for **rusting** to occur.
 
 
 
• **Other Corrosion Prevention Methods:**
 
 
• **Painting:** Creating a barrier between the metal and the atmosphere.
 
• **Oiling and Greasing:** Used frequently for moving machine parts to repel **moisture**.
 
• **Alloying:** Mixing **iron** with metals like **chromium** and **nickel** to create **stainless steel**, which does not rust.
 
• **Electroplating:** Using **electricity** to coat a metal with a thin layer of another metal like **tin** or **chromium**.
 
 
 
• **Properties of Zinc Coating:**
 
 
• When exposed to the atmosphere, **zinc** reacts with **oxygen** to form **zinc oxide**, which further reacts with **carbon dioxide** to form **zinc carbonate** (**ZnCO3**).
 
• This **zinc carbonate** layer is a strong, insoluble material that stops further corrosion of both the **zinc** and the underlying **iron**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **History:** The term is named after the **Italian** scientist **Luigi Galvani**, though the practical application of **hot-dip galvanizing** was patented later by **Stanislas Sorel** in **1837**.
 
• **Types of Galvanization:**
 
 
• **Hot-dip Galvanizing:** Submerging the metal in molten **zinc**.
 
• **Electro-galvanizing:** A layer of **zinc** is applied using an **electric current** in an electrolyte solution.
 
• **Sherardizing:** Also known as **vapor galvanizing**, it involves heating the **iron** component in a closed drum with **zinc dust**.
 
 
 
• **Industrial Use:** This method is widely used in the **construction** of bridges, **automotive** body parts, **telecommunication** towers, and household items like **buckets** and **roofing sheets**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** By extending the life of **infrastructure**, **galvanisation** saves billions of dollars annually in **maintenance** and **replacement** costs.
